en.greeting: Hi! Today is about the conversations people dread: giving bad news, speaking for your organisation in a crisis, and telling a senior person or a client that you disagree. For each one you'll get a clear structure, so you can be honest and kind at the same time.

steps.title: Bad news: say it early, say it clearly
steps.text: Quick recap: in negotiation you said no with I'm afraid + reason + alternative, and in meetings you set action points with who, what and by when. Now the hardest version: news nobody wants to hear.
steps.body: Two big mistakes: **burying** the news under ten minutes of background, and **shrinking** it. *Maybe there's a little problem with the deadline, but it's okay* (often from *ada sedikit kendala*) sounds like **no** problem, so the client keeps planning around the old date. Give the news in **one clear sentence** near the start, then: **reason** (brief, no excuses) → **impact** → **what you're doing / options** → **next step**.

pairs.en: I'm afraid I have some difficult news.
pairs.id: Mohon maaf, ada kabar kurang baik. → sinyal (satu kalimat saja)

pairs.en: We won't meet the 15 March deadline.
pairs.id: Kami tidak akan bisa memenuhi tenggat 15 Maret. → kabarnya, satu kalimat jelas

pairs.en: The steel arrived six weeks late.
pairs.id: Bajanya datang terlambat enam minggu. → alasan singkat

pairs.en: That means you can't move in before April.
pairs.id: Artinya Anda belum bisa pindah sebelum April. → dampak

pairs.en: Here's what we can do instead.
pairs.id: Ini yang bisa kami lakukan sebagai gantinya. → pilihan / solusi

pairs.en: I'll send you a new schedule by Friday.
pairs.id: Saya kirim jadwal baru paling lambat Jumat. → langkah berikutnya

steps.title: Your turn: the opening
steps.text: Which opening gets the news across clearly and early?

options: Thank you for your time. Before anything else, I want to say how hard the team has worked, and the requirements changed several times, and our vendor was late, so…
I'm afraid we won't be ready for the 1 May launch: we need three more weeks. Let me explain why, and what we can do in the meantime.
Maybe there's a small issue with the timeline, but it's okay, don't worry.
question.prompt: Dimas manages a software project for a bank in Jakarta. The bank's new app won't be ready for the 1 May launch: the team needs three more weeks. He calls the bank's IT director. Which opening is best?
question.explanation: The second opening gives the news in the first sentence (**I'm afraid we won't be ready …**) with the new timing, then promises the reason and the options. The first buries the news under excuses and blame. The third shrinks it: *a small issue … it's okay* sounds like the app will launch on time.

steps.title: Empathy, responsibility, one sorry
steps.text: Clear doesn't mean cold. Three habits make bad news easier to hear.
steps.body: **Empathy without false comfort:** show you understand the impact, but don't say *Don't worry, it'll all be fine* if you don't know that. **Responsibility with *we*:** *We made a mistake*, not *Mistakes were made* (like *telah terjadi kesalahan*, a passive hides who). **One sincere apology, then action:** five sorries sound like panic. **No blame:** *Our supplier was late, and we should have had a backup.*

pairs.en: I know this isn't what you were hoping for.
pairs.id: Saya tahu ini bukan yang Anda harapkan. → empati

pairs.en: I can imagine how frustrating this is.
pairs.id: Saya bisa membayangkan betapa menjengkelkannya ini. → empati

pairs.en: We made a mistake, and that's on us.
pairs.id: Kami melakukan kesalahan, dan itu tanggung jawab kami.

pairs.en: Our supplier was late, and we should have had a backup.
pairs.id: Pemasok kami terlambat, dan seharusnya kami punya cadangan. → alasan tanpa menyalahkan

pairs.en: I'm sorry. Here's how we'll put it right.
pairs.id: Saya minta maaf. Begini cara kami memperbaikinya. → satu maaf, lalu tindakan

steps.title: Build an empathy line
steps.text: Put the words in order to make a sentence that shows you understand the impact on the client.

question.solution: I understand this causes real problems for your team.
question.prompt: Arrange the words: Saya mengerti ini menimbulkan masalah serius bagi tim Anda.
question.explanation: **I understand + this causes + real problems + for your team**: you name the impact on *them*, without promising that everything will be fine. *Real* is stronger than *some*: it takes their problem seriously.

steps.title: Crisis: four questions
steps.text: A crisis is bad news in public, fast, with only half the facts. Four questions keep you clear.
steps.body: Every update answers: **what happened** (facts only: what you know **and** what you don't know yet), **what we're doing**, **what people should do**, and **when the next update comes** (a time, not *soon*). Short sentences. No guessing the cause. One **spokesperson** (juru bicara). If you know almost nothing yet, give a **holding statement**: you're aware, you're investigating, and when you'll update. Avoid *No comment* (sounds like hiding) and *We apologise for any inconvenience* when people are really hurt.

pairs.en: Since 8 a.m., customers haven't been able to log in.
pairs.id: Sejak pukul 08.00, nasabah tidak bisa masuk. → apa yang terjadi

pairs.en: We don't yet know the cause.
pairs.id: Kami belum tahu penyebabnya. → jujur soal yang belum diketahui

pairs.en: Our engineers are working to restore the service.
pairs.id: Teknisi kami sedang memulihkan layanan. → apa yang kami lakukan

pairs.en: In the meantime, please use our ATMs.
pairs.id: Sementara itu, silakan gunakan ATM kami. → apa yang perlu dilakukan orang

pairs.en: Our next update will be at 11 a.m.
pairs.id: Kabar berikutnya pukul 11.00. → kapan kabar berikutnya

pairs.en: We're aware of reports of … and are investigating.
pairs.id: Kami mengetahui adanya laporan … dan sedang menyelidikinya. → holding statement

steps.title: Your turn: the first statement
steps.text: Rumours are spreading, and the facts aren't known yet. What should the company say first?

options: We're aware of reports that some customer data may have been exposed, and we're investigating. We'll post an update by 3 p.m. today.
No comment at this time.
It was probably a hacker from overseas, but don't worry: your data is 100% safe.
question.prompt: Posts on social media claim that customer data from Belanjaku, an online shop in Jakarta, has leaked. The team doesn't know yet whether it's true. Which is the best first public statement?
question.explanation: The first option is a model **holding statement**: we know about the reports (**We're aware of reports …**), we're acting (**we're investigating**), and here's when we'll update (**by 3 p.m.**). *No comment* sounds like hiding. The third guesses the cause and promises *100% safe* before anyone knows: if either turns out wrong, nobody trusts the next update.

steps.title: Disagreeing upward
steps.text: From the implied-meaning lesson you know soften + reason + alternative. With a manager or a client, add evidence, and leave the final decision with them.
steps.body: Four moves: **acknowledge their goal** → **state your concern with evidence** (a number, what happened last time) → **propose an alternative** → **leave the decision with them** (*It's your call, but I'd recommend …*). Raise it privately first if you can. Respect for seniors is a strength, but *sungkan* and *asal bapak senang* (telling the boss only what pleases him) turn it into silence, and in English *Yes, Pak* sounds like full agreement. Exception: when **safety, the law or ethics** are at stake, be respectful but **direct**.

pairs.en: I can see why you want to …
pairs.id: Saya paham kenapa Bapak/Ibu ingin … → akui tujuannya

pairs.en: My concern is that …
pairs.id: Yang saya khawatirkan, … → kekhawatiran

pairs.en: Last year, the same plan cost us …
pairs.id: Tahun lalu, rencana yang sama membuat kita rugi … → bukti

pairs.en: Could we consider …?
pairs.id: Bagaimana kalau kita pertimbangkan …? → alternatif

pairs.en: It's your call, but I'd recommend …
pairs.id: Keputusannya di tangan Bapak/Ibu, tapi saran saya … → serahkan keputusan

pairs.en: Could I have five minutes after the meeting?
pairs.id: Boleh minta waktu lima menit setelah rapat? → empat mata dulu

pairs.en: I can't sign this off: it isn't safe.
pairs.id: Saya tidak bisa menyetujui ini: tidak aman. → keselamatan / etika: langsung

steps.title: Listen: the director's plan
steps.text: Your director announces a decision in a team meeting in Jakarta. Listen, then choose your reply.

question.listen: Right, everyone. I've decided we'll launch the new app on the first of November, two weeks early. The client will be delighted, and we can finish the testing after the launch. Any questions?
options: Yes, of course, Pak. Whatever you think is best.
With respect, Pak, that's a terrible plan. Testing after launch is just asking for trouble.
I can see why an early launch appeals, Pak. My worry is that last time we launched early, we had 300 bug reports in week one. Could we keep the fifteenth? It's your decision, of course.
question.prompt: Listen to Pak Hendra's announcement. You think the plan is risky. Which reply disagrees diplomatically?
question.explanation: The third reply uses all four moves: it **acknowledges** the goal (*an early launch appeals*), gives a **concern with evidence** (300 bug reports last time), proposes an **alternative** (keep the fifteenth) and **leaves the decision** with him (*It's your decision, of course*). The first is *asal bapak senang*: he'll hear full agreement. The second is clear but far too blunt for a director in front of the team, and offers no alternative.

steps.title: When to be direct
steps.text: Sometimes the soft code is the wrong tool. Which reply fits here?

options: Yes, Pak. I'll cook it now.
Pak, I can't serve this chicken. It's been at 15 degrees all night, and it isn't safe. We need to throw it away, and I'll order a fresh delivery for lunch.
I'm not sure that's the best idea, Pak. Perhaps we could think about it later?
question.prompt: In a restaurant kitchen in Surabaya, the fridge broke overnight and the chicken was at 15°C for ten hours. The regional manager, Pak Joko, says: 'It's probably fine. Cook it today, we can't waste it.' What should the head chef, Sari, say?
question.explanation: Food safety is at stake, so Sari is respectful (**Pak**) but **direct**: a clear no, the evidence (15 degrees all night) and a solution (a fresh delivery). The soft code (*I'm not sure that's the best idea … later?*) can be heard as *maybe*, and customers could get sick. *Yes, Pak* is the *asal bapak senang* trap.

steps.text: Flip each card. Say the English before you look.

steps.title: Watch and read more
steps.text: An easy video of bad-news phrases, an article with a step-by-step method, and a lesson on disagreeing politely.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita membahas percakapan yang paling bikin deg-degan: menyampaikan kabar buruk, berbicara atas nama organisasimu saat krisis, dan menyampaikan kepada atasan senior atau klien bahwa kamu tidak setuju. Untuk masing-masing kamu dapat struktur yang jelas, supaya kamu bisa jujur dan tetap baik sekaligus.

steps.title: Kabar buruk: di awal, dengan jelas
steps.text: Ulang singkat: di negosiasi kamu menolak dengan I'm afraid + alasan + alternatif, dan di rapat kamu membuat poin tindak lanjut dengan siapa, apa dan paling lambat kapan. Sekarang versi paling sulit: kabar yang tidak ingin didengar siapa pun.
steps.body: Dua kesalahan besar: **mengubur** kabarnya di bawah sepuluh menit latar belakang, dan **mengecilkannya**. *Maybe there's a little problem with the deadline, but it's okay* (sering dari *ada sedikit kendala*) terdengar seperti **tidak ada** masalah, jadi klien tetap merencanakan dengan tanggal lama. Sampaikan kabarnya dalam **satu kalimat jelas** di awal, lalu: **alasan** (singkat, tanpa dalih) → **dampak** → **apa yang kamu lakukan / pilihannya** → **langkah berikutnya**.

pairs.en: I'm afraid I have some difficult news.
pairs.id: Mohon maaf, ada kabar kurang baik. → sinyal (satu kalimat saja)

pairs.en: We won't meet the 15 March deadline.

pairs.en: The steel arrived six weeks late.

pairs.en: That means you can't move in before April.

pairs.en: I'll send you a new schedule by Friday.
pairs.id: Saya kirim jadwal baru paling lambat Jumat. → langkah berikutnya

steps.title: Giliranmu: pembukanya
steps.text: Pembuka mana yang menyampaikan kabarnya dengan jelas dan di awal?

options: Thank you for your time. Before anything else, I want to say how hard the team has worked, and the requirements changed several times, and our vendor was late, so…
I'm afraid we won't be ready for the 1 May launch: we need three more weeks. Let me explain why, and what we can do in the meantime.
Maybe there's a small issue with the timeline, but it's okay, don't worry.
question.prompt: Dimas mengelola proyek perangkat lunak untuk sebuah bank di Jakarta. Aplikasi baru bank itu tidak akan siap untuk peluncuran 1 Mei: timnya butuh tiga minggu lagi. Ia menelepon direktur TI bank tersebut. Pembuka mana yang paling tepat?
question.explanation: Pembuka kedua menyampaikan kabarnya di kalimat pertama (**I'm afraid we won't be ready …**) beserta perkiraan waktunya, lalu menjanjikan alasan dan pilihannya. Pembuka pertama mengubur kabarnya di bawah dalih dan menyalahkan pihak lain. Pembuka ketiga mengecilkannya: *a small issue … it's okay* terdengar seperti aplikasinya akan meluncur tepat waktu.

steps.title: Empati, tanggung jawab, satu maaf
steps.text: Jelas bukan berarti dingin. Tiga kebiasaan ini membuat kabar buruk lebih mudah diterima.
steps.body: **Empati tanpa penghiburan palsu:** tunjukkan kamu paham dampaknya, tapi jangan bilang *Don't worry, it'll all be fine* kalau kamu sendiri belum tahu. **Tanggung jawab dengan *we*:** *We made a mistake*, bukan *Mistakes were made* (seperti *telah terjadi kesalahan*, kalimat pasif menyembunyikan pelakunya). **Satu permintaan maaf yang tulus, lalu tindakan:** lima kali minta maaf terdengar panik. **Jangan menyalahkan:** *Our supplier was late, and we should have had a backup.*

pairs.en: I can imagine how frustrating this is.

pairs.en: We made a mistake, and that's on us.

pairs.id: Pemasok kami terlambat, dan seharusnya kami punya cadangan. → alasan tanpa menyalahkan

pairs.en: I'm sorry. Here's how we'll put it right.

steps.title: Susun kalimat empati
steps.text: Susun kata-katanya menjadi kalimat yang menunjukkan kamu paham dampaknya bagi klien.

question.solution: I understand this causes real problems for your team.
question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Saya mengerti ini menimbulkan masalah serius bagi tim Anda.
question.explanation: **I understand + this causes + real problems + for your team**: kamu menyebut dampaknya bagi *mereka*, tanpa menjanjikan semuanya akan baik-baik saja. *Real* lebih kuat daripada *some*: kamu menganggap serius masalah mereka.

steps.title: Krisis: empat pertanyaan
steps.text: Krisis adalah kabar buruk di depan publik, serba cepat, dengan fakta yang baru setengah. Empat pertanyaan ini menjaga pesanmu tetap jelas.
steps.body: Setiap kabar terbaru menjawab: **apa yang terjadi** (fakta saja: apa yang sudah kamu ketahui **dan** yang belum), **apa yang sedang kami lakukan**, **apa yang perlu dilakukan orang**, dan **kapan kabar berikutnya** (sebutkan jamnya, bukan *soon*). Kalimat pendek. Jangan menebak penyebabnya. Satu **juru bicara**. Kalau kamu hampir belum tahu apa-apa, sampaikan **holding statement** (pernyataan sementara): kamu tahu, kamu sedang menyelidiki, dan kapan kabar berikutnya. Hindari *No comment* (terdengar menyembunyikan sesuatu) dan *We apologise for any inconvenience* kalau orang benar-benar dirugikan.

pairs.en: Since 8 a.m., customers haven't been able to log in.
pairs.id: Sejak pukul 08.00, nasabah tidak bisa masuk. → apa yang terjadi

pairs.en: We don't yet know the cause.
pairs.id: Kami belum tahu penyebabnya. → jujur soal yang belum diketahui

pairs.en: Our engineers are working to restore the service.
pairs.id: Teknisi kami sedang memulihkan layanan. → apa yang kami lakukan

pairs.en: In the meantime, please use our ATMs.
pairs.id: Sementara itu, silakan gunakan ATM kami. → apa yang perlu dilakukan orang

pairs.en: Our next update will be at 11 a.m.
pairs.id: Kabar berikutnya pukul 11.00. → kapan kabar berikutnya

pairs.en: We're aware of reports of … and are investigating.
pairs.id: Kami mengetahui adanya laporan … dan sedang menyelidikinya. → holding statement

steps.title: Giliranmu: pernyataan pertama
steps.text: Kabar burung menyebar, dan faktanya belum diketahui. Apa yang sebaiknya disampaikan perusahaan lebih dulu?

options: We're aware of reports that some customer data may have been exposed, and we're investigating. We'll post an update by 3 p.m. today.
No comment at this time.
It was probably a hacker from overseas, but don't worry: your data is 100% safe.
question.prompt: Unggahan di media sosial menyebutkan data pelanggan Belanjaku, sebuah toko online di Jakarta, bocor. Timnya belum tahu apakah itu benar. Mana pernyataan publik pertama yang paling tepat?
question.explanation: Pilihan pertama adalah contoh **holding statement** yang baik: kami tahu ada laporannya (**We're aware of reports …**), kami bertindak (**we're investigating**), dan inilah kapan kabar berikutnya (**by 3 p.m.**). *No comment* terdengar seperti menyembunyikan sesuatu. Pilihan ketiga menebak penyebabnya dan menjanjikan *100% safe* sebelum ada yang tahu: kalau salah satunya ternyata keliru, tidak ada yang percaya kabar berikutnya.

steps.title: Tidak setuju dengan atasan
steps.text: Dari pelajaran makna tersirat kamu tahu: lunakkan + alasan + alternatif. Dengan atasan atau klien, tambahkan bukti, dan serahkan keputusan akhirnya kepada mereka.
steps.body: Empat langkah: **akui tujuan mereka** → **sampaikan kekhawatiran dengan bukti** (angka, kejadian sebelumnya) → **usulkan alternatif** → **serahkan keputusan** (*It's your call, but I'd recommend …*). Kalau bisa, sampaikan empat mata dulu. Menghormati atasan itu kekuatan, tapi rasa *sungkan* dan budaya *asal bapak senang* mengubahnya menjadi diam, dan dalam bahasa Inggris *Yes, Pak* terdengar seperti setuju sepenuhnya. Pengecualian: kalau **keselamatan, hukum atau etika** dipertaruhkan, tetap hormat tapi **langsung**.

pairs.id: Saya paham kenapa Bapak/Ibu ingin … → akui tujuannya

pairs.en: My concern is that …
pairs.id: Yang saya khawatirkan, … → kekhawatiran

pairs.en: Last year, the same plan cost us …
pairs.id: Tahun lalu, rencana yang sama membuat kita rugi … → bukti

steps.title: Dengarkan: rencana direktur
steps.text: Direkturmu mengumumkan keputusan dalam rapat tim di Jakarta. Dengarkan, lalu pilih jawabanmu.

question.listen: Right, everyone. I've decided we'll launch the new app on the first of November, two weeks early. The client will be delighted, and we can finish the testing after the launch. Any questions?
options: Yes, of course, Pak. Whatever you think is best.
With respect, Pak, that's a terrible plan. Testing after launch is just asking for trouble.
I can see why an early launch appeals, Pak. My worry is that last time we launched early, we had 300 bug reports in week one. Could we keep the fifteenth? It's your decision, of course.
question.prompt: Dengarkan pengumuman Pak Hendra. Menurutmu rencananya berisiko. Jawaban mana yang menyatakan tidak setuju secara diplomatis?
question.explanation: Jawaban ketiga memakai keempat langkah: **mengakui** tujuannya (*an early launch appeals*), menyampaikan **kekhawatiran dengan bukti** (300 laporan bug terakhir kali), mengusulkan **alternatif** (tetap tanggal 15) dan **menyerahkan keputusan** kepadanya (*It's your decision, of course*). Jawaban pertama adalah *asal bapak senang*: ia akan mendengar persetujuan penuh. Jawaban kedua jelas, tapi terlalu kasar untuk direktur di depan tim, dan tidak menawarkan alternatif.

steps.title: Kapan harus langsung
steps.text: Kadang kode halus justru alat yang salah. Jawaban mana yang pas di sini?

options: Yes, Pak. I'll cook it now.
Pak, I can't serve this chicken. It's been at 15 degrees all night, and it isn't safe. We need to throw it away, and I'll order a fresh delivery for lunch.
I'm not sure that's the best idea, Pak. Perhaps we could think about it later?
question.prompt: Di dapur sebuah restoran di Surabaya, kulkasnya rusak semalaman dan ayamnya berada di suhu 15°C selama sepuluh jam. Manajer regional, Pak Joko, berkata: 'It's probably fine. Cook it today, we can't waste it.' Apa yang sebaiknya dikatakan kepala koki, Sari?
question.explanation: Ini soal keamanan pangan, jadi Sari tetap hormat (**Pak**) tapi **langsung**: penolakan yang jelas, buktinya (15 derajat semalaman) dan solusinya (kiriman baru). Kode halus (*I'm not sure that's the best idea … later?*) bisa terdengar seperti *mungkin*, dan pelanggan bisa sakit. *Yes, Pak* adalah jebakan *asal bapak senang*.

steps.title: Ulasan singkat
steps.text: Balik setiap kartu. Ucapkan bahasa Inggrisnya sebelum melihat.

flashcards.front: Kabar buruk: pembuka yang jelas (tenggat 15 Maret)
flashcards.back: I'm afraid we won't meet the 15 March deadline.
signal → news → reason → impact → options → next step
We made a mistake, and that's on us.
what happened · what we're doing · what you should do · next update
We don't yet know the cause.

flashcards.front: Tidak setuju dengan atasan: empat langkah
flashcards.back: acknowledge → concern + evidence → alternative → leave the decision
Drop the soft code: be respectful but direct.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Kabar buruk, kabar krisis dan cara tidak setuju dengan atasan dalam satu halaman.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · Komunikasi berisiko tinggi
artifact.intro: Langkahnya, ungkapannya, dan hal yang perlu diwaspadai.
rows: I'm afraid I have some difficult news.
satu kalimat peringatan, bukan basa-basi panjang
We won't meet the 15 March deadline.
di awal, satu kalimat, jangan dikecilkan
The steel arrived late. That means …
Here's what we can do instead. I'll send … by Friday.
I know this isn't what you were hoping for.
We made a mistake, and that's on us.
I'm sorry. Here's how we'll put it right.
Since 8 a.m., … We don't yet know the cause.
Our engineers are … In the meantime, please …
Our next update will be at 11 a.m.
We're aware of reports of … and are investigating.
saat fakta belum ada; bukan 'No comment'
I can see why … My concern is that …
Could we consider …? It's your call, but I'd recommend …
I can't sign this off. It isn't safe.
tips: Kabar buruk: sampaikan kabarnya dalam satu kalimat jelas di awal. Jangan dikubur, jangan dikecilkan.
Krisis: apa yang terjadi, apa yang kami lakukan, apa yang perlu kamu lakukan, kapan kabar berikutnya. Fakta saja, kalimat pendek.
Tidak setuju dengan atasan: akui tujuannya, kekhawatiran + bukti, alternatif, serahkan keputusan. Keselamatan, hukum atau etika: bicara langsung.

examples.en: I'm afraid we won't meet the 15 March deadline. Here's what we can do instead.
examples.id: Mohon maaf, kami tidak akan bisa memenuhi tenggat 15 Maret. Ini yang bisa kami lakukan sebagai gantinya.

examples.en: We're sorry. This should not have happened.
examples.id: Kami minta maaf. Ini seharusnya tidak terjadi.

examples.en: We're aware of reports of a fire at our Cikarang warehouse and are investigating. We'll update you by 3 p.m.
examples.id: Kami mengetahui adanya laporan kebakaran di gudang kami di Cikarang dan sedang menyelidikinya. Kami akan memberi kabar terbaru paling lambat pukul 15.00.

examples.en: I can see why you want a national launch. My concern is the budget. Could we consider a pilot first?
examples.id: Saya paham kenapa Ibu ingin peluncuran nasional. Yang saya khawatirkan anggarannya. Bagaimana kalau uji coba dulu?

steps.title: Tonton dan baca lebih lanjut
steps.text: Video mudah tentang ungkapan kabar buruk, artikel dengan langkah-langkahnya, dan pelajaran tentang cara tidak setuju dengan sopan.
